newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Reed-Elsevier says buy ups profits.
newsitem.headline: Reed-Elsevier says buy ups profits.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch publishing group Reed-Elsevier said on Wednesday its acquisition of some 40 U.S. legal publications from Thomson Corp would immediately enhance its earnings.
"We can say that this is profit-enhancing from the start," Elsevier's deputy chairman Paul Vlek told Reuters.

Vlek said Reed-Elsevier and Thomson had agreed not to disclose the financial terms of the acquisition, but that Reed-Elsevier had obtained a good price because of Thomson's position as a forced seller.

U.S. anti-trust authorities ordered Thomson to sell off the publications, which include U.S. Supreme Court Reports, as a condition for approval of Thomson's acquisition last year of West Publishing Co in the U.S.
Vlek said Reed-Elsevier, through its Lexis-Nexis unit, and Thomson/West were the two biggest online law publishers in the U.S. with about 50 percent of the market each.
He said Thomson/West was by far the biggest U.S. law publisher in terms of print media but that Reed-Elsevier was a small but growing hard-copy law publisher in the U.S.
The titles to be acquired from West generated sales revenues of $49 million in 1996 and were already distributed electronically through Lexis-Nexis.
Vlek said the deal with West also included the acquisition of its Auto-Cite software which would enable lawyers to find legal citations they needed within Lexis-Nexis more easily.
Under the agreement Reed-Elsevier will also obtain a five-year extension to its licence for three non-legal databases owned by Thomson: Investext, ASAP and Predicast.
